newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil mulls reuse of N. Sea Tommeliten facility.
newsitem.headline: Statoil mulls reuse of N. Sea Tommeliten facility.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS said on Thursday it may reuse subsea installations on the Tommeliten oilfield if renewed drilling in the area is successful.

The North Sea Tommeliten field is due to cease oil and gas production in 1998 but Statoil plans to spud a well in block 1/9 -- the first well for 15 years -- in 1997. Output currently flows from the Gamma Cretaceous formation.
The company has until June to submit proposals for Tommeliten's infrastructure once production has ceased.
"By then, the new well will have tested possible reserves in the Alpha Jurrassic prospect," Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.
Statoil said that if a find was made from the new well it could use the Tommeliten installation to inject gas from the new reservoir into the depleted Gamma Cretaceous reservoir.
